assistant.texte: This week the firm has: today a phone call with James DURAND (9.30 am) and the possession hearing in KERVILAC v ORLANDEC (2 pm, Valbrune County Court); tomorrow the signing of the ORLANDEC share purchase agreement (10 am) and the GDPR meeting with MARTIN Logistics; in two days' time the expert site inspection at the ZORVAL warehouse; on Friday the DURAND Holdings annual general meeting. The case management conference in DURAND v MARTIN follows next week.

Matter DURAND v MARTIN (Claim No. VB24C01234, Valbrune County Court): DURAND Building Ltd claims £48,600 including VAT as the balance due for refurbishment works. MARTIN Property Ltd disputes practical completion and seeks expert evidence. The practical completion certificate signed by both parties (document 02) contradicts that position. Next step: a reply to the defence before the case management conference; the client has sent the site meeting minutes.

The email “Change of bank details – urgent” shows the signs of a bank-detail change fraud: an unknown sender posing as ZORVAL Distribution, a domain different from the client's, a request for discretion, urgency and an account the firm has never used. Make no transfer; check by telephone with Sophie ZORVAL, on the number the firm already holds.

For KERVILAC Properties Ltd, the lease of the High Street unit expires in six months. Under the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954, the rent on renewal is assessed at open market value; to justify a higher figure, gather evidence of how the area has changed (for example the arrival of the tram line, footfall, comparable lettings) before serving a section 25 notice proposing a new lease.

ORLANDEC Ltd share sale: the buyer's solicitors want the cap on warranty claims raised to 30% of the price. Signing is scheduled for tomorrow at 10 am. Open points: the warranty cap and de minimis threshold, and two customer contracts terminable on a change of control.

ZORVAL Distribution v ORLANDEC Trading (Claim No. VB24C01302): default judgment for £12,450 has been entered and the High Court Enforcement Officer has served a notice of enforcement. The debtor has seven clear days to pay; failing payment, the enforcement agent may take control of goods.

Today: two messages from James DURAND about the defence (documents requested, completion certificate attached), a CE-File notice of hearing in DURAND v MARTIN, a fraudulent change-of-bank-details email not to be acted on, and chasers from ZORVAL Distribution and KERVILAC Properties. Three draft replies are waiting for review.
